Description: Contribute genuinely to existing communities before starting your own. Answer questions help people share knowledge.
Do: Join 3-5 communities where your audience hangs out. Be helpful for 4 weeks before mentioning your product.
Dont: Don't drop links to your product on day 1. Don't spam. Don't treat communities as marketing channels.
Giantiny_Note: Giantiny ① Customer Zero — you ARE the community member
Example: Pieter Levels helped nomads before building NomadList

Description: Create Discord/forum when you have 50+ engaged users. Not before. Empty communities are worse than no community.
Do: Wait until users ASK for a community space. Then create it with 3-5 channels max.
Dont: Don't create Discord at day 1 with 30 empty channels. Don't over-structure.
Example: Linear started with invite-only Slack. Exclusivity = quality.

Description: Your first 10 active community members are worth 1000 lurkers. Know them by name. Feature their work.
Do: DM each of your first 10 active members. Ask what they're building. Feature them.
Dont: Don't treat early members like numbers. Don't ignore their feedback.
Example: Notion's first community members became template creators → MOAT

Description: Enable users to create and share their work using your product. Templates showcases tutorials — users marketing FOR you.
Do: Create a #showcase channel. Feature best user creations weekly. Create template submission process.
Dont: Don't control everything. Don't reject contributions. Let community creativity flow.
Giantiny_Note: Giantiny ⑤ Micro-MOAT — user content = network effect
Example: Figma Community — thousands of user templates/plugins. #1 MOAT

Description: Let experienced users help newcomers. Reduces your support burden. Builds social bonds.
Do: Create helper/contributor role. Recognize top helpers publicly. Build FAQ from common Qs.
Dont: Don't abandon moderation. Don't let toxic behavior slide. Don't rely 100% on community for support.
Giantiny_Note: Giantiny ③ — community does support = code ≈ people
Example: Stack Overflow model: community answers > official support

Description: Weekly or monthly rituals keep community alive. AMA show-and-tell office hours challenge.
Do: Pick 1 ritual. Do it consistently. Weekly is better than monthly. Keep it short (30 min).
Dont: Don't create 5 events nobody attends. Don't skip weeks (consistency > intensity).
Giantiny_Note: Consistency beats grandeur — same time same place every week
Example: Indie Hackers weekly milestones thread — same format every week = habit

Description: Channel community feedback directly into product decisions. Public roadmap with voting.
Do: Use Canny or GitHub Issues for feature voting. Share reasoning when you build OR don't build something.
Dont: Don't promise every feature requested. Don't ignore feedback either. Explain tradeoffs.
Giantiny_Note: Community feels ownership → switching costs ↑ → MOAT ⑤
Example: Linear's public changelog + GitHub issues = transparent product development

Description: Turn community members into content creators. Guest posts interviews co-created tutorials.
Do: Invite active members to write guest posts or be interviewed. Give them platform and credit.
Dont: Don't exploit free labor. Always give credit. Don't edit their voice out.
Giantiny_Note: Other people create marketing content for you — ultimate Giantiny ③ leverage
Example: Buffer's transparency blog: employees + community write the content

Description: Code of conduct from day 1. Swift moderation of toxic behavior. Zero tolerance for harassment.
Do: Write 5 simple rules. Pin them. Enforce consistently. Remove bad actors within 24 hours.
Dont: Don't ignore toxicity hoping it'll resolve. Don't wait until you have a PR crisis.
Giantiny_Note: One toxic member can destroy a community of 1000. Act fast.
Example: React community CoC — clear simple well-enforced

Description: Track: DAU/MAU ratio messages/day new members/week retention. Healthy = DAU/MAU > 20%.
Do: Monthly health check: active members growth engagement quality of conversations.
Dont: Don't optimize for size over engagement. 100 active > 10000 lurkers.
Giantiny_Note: Vanity: member count. Real: messages per active member per week.
Example: Indie Hackers: 1.5M members but engagement metrics matter more
